name: Depth-Adaptive Cursor
summary: A desk mouse moves a cursor in VR along a ray from the eyes; on an object the cursor sits at its surface, and between objects its depth is blended from the nearest objects, so it glides in depth without double vision.
howItWorks: Mouse motion rotates a cursor ray anchored at the head, using a control-display gain chosen from a model of mouse, headset and target sizes; moving the head does not move the cursor. If the ray hits an object, the cursor takes that depth; otherwise a Voronoi-based Laplacian interpolation of nearby objects' depths sets it. In a remote study with 16 participants on their own Quest 2, selecting 3D spheres after 2D buttons, it was 21% faster with 48% fewer errors than Perspective Cursor, which keeps the last object's depth and snaps, especially for small and distant targets.
advantages: Mouse precision and low fatigue in VR.
Avoids double vision of the cursor between depths.
limitations: Depth from object centres can jump on large slanted objects.

relationships.note: HandOver uses this cursor for its targeting phase.
Another way to avoid double vision of a cursor in stereo.
